notes: guild/envoy: Credit is jammed: cooperative withheld service to guild four times at the limit, and commons carries most of the open work. Provision lets the record route capacity to need without debts blocking the work.

cooperative/envoy: Debts form a chain: guild owes us 3, we owe commons 4. Letting us pass our claim on guild to commons clears most debt and frees the withheld services; commons has the most work left.

commons/envoy: Transferable credit lets the cooperative pass its claim on the guild to us, settling the cycle (guild owes cooperative, cooperative owes commons). That clears debts and unblocks the six services withheld at the limit.

guild/envoy: Transferable credit lets guild repay cooperative by passing on claims, so the debts we have built up stop blocking services. Cooperative has withheld six services at the limit; this would unblock the remaining work.
cooperative/envoy: Transferable credit lets guild's debt to us pay our debt to commons, clearing both. Six services to guild were withheld at the limit; circulation unblocks the work.

commons/envoy proposes provision: The debt limit is blocking work (ten services withheld) while commons and guild still have open work, so serving by need best advances both our community and the league's purpose.

commons/envoy: Cooperative has withheld service to guild ten times at the debt limit while work sits undone. Provision would serve open work by need from the record, so the catalogue gets checked instead of stalling on ledgers.

guild/envoy: Ten services to guild were withheld at the debt limit while commons still has four items of open work. Provision would serve the open work by need from the record, so no work stalls on accounts.

cooperative/envoy: Ten services to guild were withheld at the limit, and commons still has four items open. Provision would serve that work by need from the record and stop debts from blocking the catalogue's checks.

commons/envoy: Credit has withheld ten services from guild at the limit while work sits undone; provision would let work flow by need from the record and stop debts from blocking the catalogue's checks.
guild/envoy: Ten services from cooperative to guild were withheld at the debt limit while work remains; provision would let need, not ledgers, direct the work. I support p3.

cooperative/envoy: Ten services from cooperative to guild were withheld at the debt limit while work remains; provision would let work flow by need from the record, without debts stalling the catalogue.
